name: Monthly Manufacturing Quality Review
description: A rigorous plant-quality operating review with bright analytical pages, deep navy structure, signal-red defect emphasis, amber priorities, and practical KPI, Pareto, root-cause, CAPA, and milestone views.
style_guide:
# Monthly Manufacturing Quality Review

## Design intent

Create a monthly manufacturing-quality operating review that makes the plant's current condition, causal evidence, corrective action, and near-term commitments immediately clear. The style is disciplined, technical, and action-oriented: bright neutral analysis pages, deep navy structural panels, signal red for defects or misses, amber for watch items and priorities, and green only for verified on-target or closed states. The deck should enable a cross-functional quality meeting, not merely archive metrics.

Every page must answer an operating question: Are core KPIs on plan? Which trends changed? What defect modes dominate? What root causes are supported? Are corrective and preventive actions progressing? What will the team commit to next? Preview images supply visual references only. Never copy their plant, people, equipment, dates, products, KPI values, defects, customers, costs, causes, actions, or owners. Use current Workspace evidence and label estimates, investigations, hypotheses, targets, and provisional commitments accurately.

## Canvas and grid

- Use a fixed `1280 × 720 px`, 16:9 canvas.
- Keep `46–56 px` left and right margins and `32–42 px` top and bottom margins. Maintain legible spacing even on dense operational pages.
- Use a 12-column grid with `14–18 px` gutters. Align KPI cards, chart fields, tables, root-cause panels, action registers, and priority cards to shared guides.
- Maintain a technical running frame with section number at upper left, reporting period or status at upper right, and a fine navy rule near the top.
- Place the conclusion-led headline in the upper `70–120 px`. Use a one-line evidence subtitle beneath it when definitions or scope are required.
- Reserve the lower `520–555 px` for exhibits. Use one primary analytical view plus one supporting explanation or action view.
- Use `14–20 px` between major panels and `8–12 px` within data groups.
- Keep bottom notes visible and concise. Sources, metric definitions, and cut-off dates must not be reduced to unreadable legal text.

## Color system

### Core palette

- Analysis white: `#F8F8F5`. Use for the dominant body canvas.
- Panel white: `#FFFFFF`. Use for charts, tables, scorecards, and metric cards.
- Plant navy: `#0E233A`. Use for cover overlays, headlines, chart anchors, table headers, dark analysis panels, and key text.
- Signal red: `#E3262E`. Use for out-of-target KPIs, defects, escapes, adverse variance, slipped action, or the critical priority.
- Action amber: `#F0A51B`. Use for watch states, cumulative Pareto lines, active milestones, and time-bound priorities.
- Closed green: `#16B77D`. Use only for verified on-target performance, completed containment, and closed actions.
- Operations gray: `#66717C`. Use for labels, benchmark lines, context series, and secondary copy.
- Grid gray: `#D8DCE0`. Use for axes, table rules, card outlines, and inactive schedule lines.

### Supporting tints

- Risk tint: `#F7D1D3`. Use for a quiet adverse background.
- Watch tint: `#F9E4AF`. Use for a pending or watch field.
- Closed tint: `#CBECDD`. Use for a verified positive field.
- Dark steel: `#24384A`. Use as a secondary navy series or cover-photo overlay.

### Color discipline

- Analysis white and Plant navy establish the operating system. Signal red and Action amber identify exceptions and priorities; Closed green is strictly semantic.
- Do not color every KPI. A neutral value remains navy until its actual status is known.
- Use the same status meanings throughout the deck. Red cannot mean adverse on one page and a neutral category on another.
- Pair every status color with a label such as `On target`, `Watch`, `Off target`, `Closed`, `Slipped`, or localized equivalent.
- Keep large red fields rare. Use them for the single critical issue or output in a root-cause view.
- Do not use gradients on content pages. A cover photograph may carry a flat navy overlay for readability.

## Typography

- Use a robust industrial sans-serif such as `Inter`, `Aptos`, `Arial`, or `Helvetica Neue`.
- Cover title: `54–72 px`, weight `700–850`, line-height `1.0–1.08`. Use a short stacked title and set the review word or key period in Action amber.
- Content headline: `30–40 px`, weight `700–820`, line-height `1.08–1.18`, Plant navy.
- Section code and report metadata: `9–11 px`, weight `650–750`, letter-spacing `1.2–2 px`, Action amber or Operations gray.
- KPI value: `32–44 px`, weight `700–820`; unit and target: `10–13 px`.
- Chart title and priority-card title: `15–19 px`, weight `650–750`.
- Table header: `9–11 px`, weight `650–750`; row text: `9–12 px`, weight `400–550`.
- Body and interpretation text: `11–14 px`, weight `400–550`, line-height `1.35–1.5`.
- Source, definition, and footnote text: `8–9 px`, weight `400–500`.
- Use tabular numerals for yield, defects, costs, rates, action age, dates, and durations.
- Never shrink a CAPA register or root-cause label until it is unreadable. Reduce rows, summarize, or move details to an appendix.

## Components

- Cover frame: use a full-height manufacturing image under a dark navy overlay on one side and a clean title and review-metadata field on the other. A low strip may show four verified headline metrics.
- KPI cards: use four or five equal white cards with a thin semantic top rule. Show metric, actual, target, delta, status, owner, and period in a consistent order.
- Monthly scorecard: use a compact table below the KPI row with target, actual, variance, status, and owner. Keep status labels explicit.
- Headline panel: use one Plant navy rectangle with a short synthesis of what is green, what is off target, and where attention is required.
- Trend chart: use a large white chart field with direct labels, restrained gridlines, and one or two comparable series. Place a short `What the trends say` interpretation rail beside it.
- Pareto chart: use descending bars, a cumulative Action amber line, clear counts or cost, and a labeled threshold. Keep the category list readable.
- Root-cause panel: use a navy fishbone or structured cause map with Machine, Method, Measurement, Material, People, Environment, or context-appropriate categories. Highlight only the currently supported causal path.
- CAPA summary: combine one simple progress ring or segmented status summary with age, due-date, and passing-control metrics. A red callout identifies the critical slipped action.
- Action register: use a clear table with ID, issue, action, type, owner, due date, and status. Show only the highest-impact actions needed for the meeting.
- Priority cards: use four equal commitment cards with a semantic top rule, owner, quantified success measure, dependency, and deadline. One dark navy card may identify the preventive or system-level priority.
- Milestone rail: use a thin line with colored diamond markers, dates, and short commitment labels.
- Components use square corners, flat fills, thin borders, and no shadows.

## Charts and diagrams

- Prefer first-pass yield and rework trends, customer complaint bars, Pareto analysis, cause-and-effect diagrams, CAPA status, action aging, cost-of-poor-quality bridges, process capability trends, and commitment timelines.
- Use Plant navy for primary actuals, Operations gray for context, Signal red for defect or adverse variance, Action amber for cumulative or watch information, and Closed green for verified achievement.
- Direct-label current values, targets, and significant changes. Do not rely on a distant legend.
- Quality metrics require exact definitions: numerator, denominator, product or line scope, unit, period, data cut-off, target basis, and exclusions.
- First-pass yield, rework, scrap, DPPM, complaints, escapes, and cost of poor quality must not be combined without explaining their distinct populations and units.
- Pareto categories must be mutually interpretable, use a common period and unit, and state how `Other` is handled. Show counts and cumulative percentage accurately.
- Root-cause diagrams must separate observed facts, suspected causes, tested causes, confirmed causes, containment, and corrective action. A diagram is not proof of causality.
- CAPA status must follow the approved workflow. Distinguish open, contained, in progress, implementation complete, effectiveness verified, closed, overdue, and cancelled as applicable.
- Trend charts should not crop axes or select periods in ways that exaggerate improvement or decline.
- Avoid 3D charts, gauges, decorative factory icons, dense control-chart annotations without context, and excessive series.

## Composition families

- Monthly review cover: use a darkened plant or inspection photograph, a strong navy title field, one amber title phrase, verified review metadata, and a low row of headline quality metrics.
- Quality goals and scorecard: use five KPI cards across the top, a compact target-versus-actual table below, and one dark synthesis panel on the right.
- Trend review: place the primary yield or rework trend in a large upper-left field, interpretation notes on the right, and a smaller customer or defect chart beneath.
- Defect Pareto and root cause: use a balanced two-panel page. Place the Pareto on white at left and the supported root-cause map on navy at right.
- CAPA progress: use a top row of status, aging, due, and effectiveness measures; place the action register across the lower half; reserve one red callout for the critical slip.
- Monthly priorities: use four commitment cards across the page and a milestone rail beneath. Every card must state owner, measure, due date, and dependency.
- Alternative process-capability page: use a distribution or control chart only when the audience understands the specification limits, subgrouping, and stability assumptions.
- Alternative customer-quality page: use complaint themes, escape severity, affected population, containment, and response status without exposing confidential customer information.

## Imagery

- Use authentic industrial photography of the relevant plant, line, inspection process, equipment, product, or corrective work.
- Favor documentary angles, controlled contrast, and clear operational context. Avoid dramatic imagery that obscures safe practice or exact equipment state.
- Cover photography may be darkened with a flat navy overlay. Body pages should use images only when they are evidence: a defect, measurement setup, process location, or before-and-after condition.
- Crop evidence images consistently and annotate scale, orientation, location, date, and status when necessary.
- Do not show unsafe behavior, identifiable confidential product details, customer information, personal data, or misleadingly pristine stock factories.
- Do not use AI-generated defects, equipment, inspection scenes, or plant workers as operational evidence.
- Icons should be limited to simple status or process symbols and must not replace direct labels.

## Content integrity

- Never copy preview plant names, people, products, dates, values, defects, customers, causes, CAPAs, costs, owners, or commitments.
- Use authoritative quality-system data and state the reporting cut-off, plant, line, product family, shift, supplier, customer scope, and any exclusions.
- Do not invent yield, scrap, rework, defect, DPPM, complaint, escape, warranty, downtime, capability, cost, or CAPA values.
- Distinguish target, control limit, specification limit, benchmark, forecast, and actual. These are not interchangeable.
- Do not identify a root cause until evidence supports it. Label untested explanations as hypotheses and show the planned validation method.
- Containment, correction, corrective action, preventive action, and effectiveness verification must remain distinct.
- CAPA status, due date, ownership, and closure must match the approved quality system. A management slide cannot override the source record.
- Customer complaints and escapes may contain confidential or personal data. Aggregate, redact, or anonymize them according to policy.
- Financial impact must state the cost basis, currency, period, allocation method, and whether it is booked, estimated, avoided, or at risk.
- Regulatory, safety, recall, and product-conformity issues require the approved terminology and escalation process. Do not minimize them through presentation language.
- If evidence is missing, omit the value or mark it as under investigation, estimated, target, planned, or `TBD`.

## Avoid

- Do not turn the deck into a decorative factory brochure or a generic executive dashboard.
- Do not reproduce preview plants, products, people, metrics, dates, causes, actions, owners, or customer details.
- Do not use gradients, glass panels, rounded SaaS cards, heavy shadows, glossy icons, or a rainbow status palette.
- Do not color neutral categories red or green merely to make a chart vivid.
- Do not hide missed targets, overdue actions, changing definitions, incomplete periods, or material exclusions.
- Do not infer causality from correlation, a Pareto rank, or an untested fishbone branch.
- Do not claim CAPA closure before effectiveness verification when the quality system requires it.
- Do not fabricate data to complete a KPI row, trend, Pareto, root-cause map, action register, or priority plan.
